eips.title: Optional Execution Proofs
eips.summary: Extensive discussion of CFI status for Hegota, spec readiness, PR line counts, CL implementation progress, and Sepolia deployment plans.

moments.context: Ignacio announced that EIP-8025 will likely be proposed for CFI in Hegota at the next ACDC call, urging supporters to attend.
Ignacio noted he updated the EIP-8025 document with latest progress and arguments, emphasizing the effort's maturity and readiness.
Ignacio said removing the headers field also retires a lot of the 8025 test cases that exist today for invalid header lists.
Ignacio presented a table showing EIP-8025's PR is 17,000 lines total but only 56 lines touch the STF spec, with most lines being tests and framework changes.
Ignacio described a new EIP for get-payload-with-witness for block building, noting it is not strictly needed for EIP-8025 but complements the long-term mandatory proofs arc.
Francesco described rebasing EIP-8025 on the Gloas specs and plans to deploy a prover on Sepolia, inviting client teams to join testing.

Manu reported Prysm implemented EIP-8025 as a proof of concept, working on Kurtosis, and is running a verifier node on Sepolia but encountering an incompatibility with Lighthouse sending proofs of type 0.

eips.title: Read BLOCKHASH from Storage and Update Cost
eips.summary: Announced as CFI'd in the last ACDE call, simplifying stateless inputs by moving BLOCKHASH to EIP-2935 system contract.

moments.context: Ignacio announced EIP-7709 was CFI'd in the last ACDE call and explained it simplifies the execution witness by removing the headers field, since BLOCKHASH now uses the EIP-2935 system contract.
Ignacio noted EIP-7709 eliminates many test cases around invalid header lists and is a step toward the long-term direction where the execution witness is mainly state tree nodes.

eips.title: Serve historical block hashes from state
eips.summary: Referenced as the system contract that EIP-7709 uses to serve BLOCKHASH from state.

moments.context: Ignacio explained that EIP-7709 makes BLOCKHASH use the EIP-2935 system contract, so block hash data moves into the state tree.
